title: Hugging Face shares the production design behind the revived Papers with Code search
friendlyTitle: How Papers with Code built a search system that keeps working
summary: Hugging Face explains how Papers with Code searches more than 110,000 papers using PostgreSQL full-text retrieval, pgvector semantic search and reciprocal-rank fusion. Its design separates batch embedding work from live queries and falls back to keyword search when the embedding endpoint is unavailable.
friendlySummary: Hugging Face combines exact word search with meaning-based search across more than 110,000 papers. If the AI search service is unavailable, the system can still use normal text search.
whyItMatters: The architecture is a useful blueprint for dependable research search and RAG systems: version embedding inputs, move expensive work offline and keep a simpler fallback path. It also gives researchers and agents a practical way to find papers and related artifacts through the site or CLI.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This is a helpful design for anyone building document search. A simple backup method can keep the service useful when the smarter part has a problem.
